title: The Veil of the Ninefold Court
premise: Paloma Thackeray, a scribe indentured to the valley's memory-temple, discovers the mute child at her door speaks in the lost tongue of the Ninefold Court — and that his soul was sold there by her own mother, a debt Paloma never knew existed. Leaving the valley where magic cannot follow, she descends beneath the mountain with thirteen turns of the moon to bargain, steal, or cheat her way back what was sold. Each truth she recovers costs her a memory of home, forcing her to choose between loyalty to the people who raised her and the truth of who sold whom. In the end, Paloma wins the child's soul back by surrendering her own name to the Court, returning home remembered by no one — until the child, restored, speaks her name aloud and gives it back.
about_author: Ines Pemberton is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing orphaned manuscripts before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted chapel on the coast, where she insists the tide keeps better secrets than any archive.

chapters.title: The Child Who Spoke Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A silent child appears at the temple door during a debt-audit, speaking a language no living scholar knows — yet Paloma finds herself half-understanding it. The temple elders demand he be turned out; Paloma hides him instead. Emotional beat: quiet defiance awakening in a woman trained to obey.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Translating the child's words through old ledgers, she uncovers a contract bearing her mother's signature: one soul, sold to the court beneath the mountain. The valley's magic-dead soil suddenly feels less like safety and more like exile. Emotional beat: the ground of her identity cracking open.

chapters.title: The Debt-Bound Depart
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Her indenture forbids leaving; breaking it forfeits everything she owns, including her name in the temple rolls. She goes anyway, smuggling the child out in a grain cart past wardens who smell magic like rot. Emotional beat: terror braided with exhilaration at first freedom.

chapters.title: Road of Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with the child, Wren, whose fragmented memories surface as they travel toward the mountain. They fall in with a caravan of soul-brokers who trade in exactly what Paloma needs — and exactly what she fears. Emotional beat: wary trust forming between two strangers bound by one crime.

chapters.title: The Broker's Honest Lie
chapters.summary: Caravan-master Odile's POV. Odile offers passage beneath the mountain in exchange for one of Paloma's memories — the first payment the Court will accept at its gate. Paloma pays with the day her mother died, and cannot remember why she weeps. Emotional beat: grief without its cause; the price becomes real.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain, Above the Law
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Ninefold Court receives them with velvet courtesy; nine masked sovereigns each claim a piece of every visitor's story. Paloma learns her mother didn't sell Wren's soul — she traded her own daughter's future to buy the child time. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted into unbearable love.

chapters.title: What the Ninth Mask Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The ninth sovereign recognizes Wren — he is the Court's abandoned heir, his soul sold away so he could never claim the throne. The moon nears its thirteenth turn; the Court moves to erase them both. Emotional beat: a child choosing, for the first time, what he wants to be.

chapters.title: The Theft of a Soul
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During the Court's masquerade of debts, Paloma steals Wren's soul-vessel from the vault of names, trading memory after memory as toll — her village, her teacher, her own face. Odile betrays them at the gate, then relents. Emotional beat: sacrifice made luminous by what it protects.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Cornered in the Court's heart as the moon completes its cycle, Paloma offers the only currency left: her entire name, her place in every record ever written. The sovereigns accept. Wren's soul returns to him as Paloma dissolves from all remembrance. Emotional beat: triumph and erasure in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Name Given Back
chapters.summary: Resolution, Wren's POV. Home in the valley, Wren — whole, speaking plainly now — stands before a woman who tends the temple garden and knows neither him nor herself. He speaks her name aloud, the one word the Court could not unmake because he carried it inside his returned soul. Memory begins its slow return. Emotional beat: love as an act of restoration.
